answer.rationale: Rolling back is excluded by the compliance constraint on the security patch, so memory b1 is not load-bearing here. The symptom — write-path p99 climbing for 90 minutes, confined to the primary region, with settlement traffic at peak — points away from a read-replica routing issue (memory b5) since the degradation is on writes, not reads. Add_capacity does not address a regional fault pattern and risks masking it; enable_circuit_breaker on an upstream dependency (memory b4) would also shed legitimate settlement writes during peak, which conflicts with the primary objective of maximizing sustained availability without losing customer writes. Regional failover (memory b2) directly addresses the primary-region localization of the latency, shifts writes to a healthy region where headroom was provisioned (memory b3 supports this), and preserves write availability at peak. Memory b2 is the one I want verified before committing — I want to confirm the failover cleanly drained traffic and error rates recovered within minutes in the prior incident, since I'm betting sustained peak-load writes on that same pattern.
